coding_protocol.attention_view: One signed/permuted 96-way Hadamard view. Pad final group to 96 when needed; fold and normalize each row. All actual input features enter every coordinate; padded groups can break exact row orthogonality.
coding_protocol.input: Embedding plus all previous 96D post-attention and raw 512D KS2 states; no detach. Latest previous residual is already included once in this history.
coding_protocol.branches: One shared LayerNorm then one 608-row fixed matrix multiply. First 512 coordinates undergo coordinate-wise causal time mix then geometry only; final 96 feed normalized RWKV with view+update residual. No same-layer attention-to-KS2 projection. Dynamic arm appends 8 control rows to that same matrix multiply. These pass through a separate rank-8 KS2 cell; its eight activations weight eight learned 608D vectors. Normalize the resulting gains to unit RMS over all 608 main outputs before multiplying them into the main mux outputs.
coding_protocol.output: The 96 attention channels pass through the decoder unchanged alongside the 512 KS2 channels. Only the final full 608D residual demuxes to 96D, then output norm/head. No intermediate demux or attention pass-through between layers.

mux_gains.placement: Output of shared mux, before splitting the main KS2 and RWKV branches.
mux_gains.formula: z = KS2(extra_rank8_view); g = z @ V; gain = g / sqrt(max(mean(g*g),1e-8)); output = main_mux_output * gain
mux_gains.normalization: Per token, across all 608 main output coordinates, unit RMS.
mux_gains.vector_initialization: Normal(0, 1/sqrt(8)); independent seed+3000 RNG; dynamic arm changes the initial function.
mux_gains.history: Only the original 608 main outputs enter history. Control subspace is local to its layer, with no separate time mix.
mux_gains.gradient_initialization: Nonzero random vectors allow immediate gradients to the extra KS2 geometry.

architecture: Single layer-entry mux with 64x8 KS2, one 96D RWKV view and one extra rank-8 KS2 gain modulator; final full-residual demux
